title: Static-host (GitHub Pages) QR pairing
summary: Fixes phone pairing when the app is served from a public static host (GitHub Pages under a base path) instead of a local Vite dev server. Root cause: `buildPhoneUrl` built the offer-QR URL from the Settings LAN IP + a `/phone` path, so on the Pages origin (https:, empty port) the QR encoded `https://<lanIp>/phone` — port 443 on a machine with nothing listening — and the phone hung on a blank page; even pointed correctly, `/<repo>/phone` 404s on a static host with no SPA fallback, and `main.tsx`'s `^/phone` route detection never matched a base path. Fix (decision-memo §'Phase 2b.5'): the offer QR now reflects the laptop's CURRENT origin + base path and carries the phone role + offer in the hash (`<origin><base>#role=phone&offer=<payload>`), so the request always resolves to the served index.html — no 404.html, no SPA fallback, no change to .github/workflows/pages.yml. `buildPhoneUrl(location, lanIp, payload)` now: uses the origin verbatim on any deployed host (LAN IP irrelevant); on a loopback host (localhost/127.0.0.1/::1) swaps in the Settings LAN IP keeping the dev port, returning null (→ manual fallback) when none is set. `isPhoneRoute(location)` (new, in pair-url.ts) selects the companion via the hash marker OR the legacy `/phone` path (backward compatible); `main.tsx` consumes it. `parsePhoneFragment` now also returns the `role`. Review-driven hardening: (M5) the offer QR is sized against the assembled URL via `fitsSingleQr`/`QR_MAX_URL_BYTES` (1273), not the payload alone, since the Pages prefix is much longer than `…:5173/phone`; (M4/M7) the phone calls `history.replaceState` after capturing the offer to drop `offer=` (the SDP embeds private LAN IPs) from the URL/history while keeping `#role=phone` so a reload re-mounts the companion; (B2/M8) `PairScreen` shows a `connect-timeout` diagnostic banner after ~20s in-flight without connect, explaining the same-Wi-Fi / no-client-isolation / no-TURN requirement. SettingsScreen + SETUP_IOS.md updated (Pages users skip the mkcert ceremony — the public origin is already trusted HTTPS, so iOS DeviceMotion works without it). Accepted scope: the WebRTC DataChannel stays peer-to-peer with STUN only (no TURN) → same non-isolated LAN only; cross-network pairing is out of scope and surfaced by the diagnostic. This is a post-completion deployment fix; the MVP feature set (phase-6.3) remains complete. Lint + tsc + vitest (289, +18) + vite build all clean; main bundle +0.38 KB gzip (under the +1 KB budget).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Offer QR encodes the laptop's current origin + base path with role + offer in the hash; resolves to served index.html with no 404.html / SPA fallback / Pages-workflow change.
acceptance_criteria.verified_by: `app/src/phone/pair-url.ts:buildPhoneUrl` assembles `${protocol}//${host}${port}${pathname}#role=phone[&offer=...]` from the passed `PhoneLocation`. `pair-url.test.ts` 'on a deployed host, uses the origin + base path verbatim …' asserts `https://www.aaroncaswell.com/pointfight-reactor/#role=phone&offer=PAYLOAD` (would fail if reverted to the old `/phone`+LAN-IP shape — this is the regression test for the original 404/hang bug). `.github/workflows/pages.yml` and `vite.config.ts` (base: './') are unchanged.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Loopback hosts swap in the Settings LAN IP (port preserved); null when unset → manual fallback. Deployed hosts use the origin verbatim and ignore the LAN IP.
acceptance_criteria.verified_by: `pair-url.test.ts`: 'on a loopback dev host, swaps in the LAN IP and keeps the port', 'on a loopback dev host with no LAN IP, returns null', 'treats 127.0.0.1 as loopback too', 'treats IPv6 loopback (::1 and [::1]) as loopback', 'on a deployed host … ignores the LAN IP'. `PairScreen.tsx` calls `buildPhoneUrl(window.location, ip||null, enc.payload)` and falls back to manual mode when it returns null.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: main.tsx selects the phone companion via isPhoneRoute, matching the hash marker OR the legacy /phone path.
acceptance_criteria.verified_by: `main.tsx` imports and uses `isPhoneRoute(window.location)`. `pair-url.test.ts` 'isPhoneRoute' block covers `/phone`, `/phone/`, the hash marker on a base path, the no-marker negative, and the `/telephone` false-positive guard. verify-phase-2b5.mjs C1 (hash marker → phone UI), C2 (no marker → laptop app), C3 (legacy /phone → phone UI) all PASS.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Phone strips offer= from the URL after capture but keeps #role=phone.
acceptance_criteria.verified_by: `PhoneApp.tsx:stripOfferFromUrl()` calls `history.replaceState(null,'',`${pathname}${search}#role=phone`)`, invoked synchronously in the offer-consume effect. verify-phase-2b5.mjs C4 PASS asserts `window.location.hash === '#role=phone'` (offer= removed) after loading `#role=phone&offer=<valid>`.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Offer QR sized against the assembled URL length, not payload alone; over-long URL → manual fallback.
acceptance_criteria.verified_by: `qr.ts` adds `QR_MAX_URL_BYTES=1273` + `fitsSingleQr(url)`. `qr.test.ts` 'fitsSingleQr' block: accepts at/under ceiling, rejects over ceiling, and 'measures the whole URL, not just the payload' (a threshold-sized payload + long prefix overflows and is rejected). `PairScreen.tsx` checks `fitsSingleQr(url)` after building and falls back to manual paste with a byte-count reason.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: PairScreen shows a connection-timeout diagnostic after ~20s in-flight without connect; scope documented as same non-isolated LAN, no TURN.
acceptance_criteria.verified_by: `PairScreen.tsx` effect arms a `CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS` (20000) timer while in-flight (scanning-answer / connecting / gathering_answer) and not connected, rendering `data-testid="connect-timeout"` with same-Wi-Fi / guest-isolation / no-relay guidance. Scope recorded in decision-memo §'Phase 2b.5' (red-team B2) and surfaced in docs/SETUP_IOS.md + the Settings hint. Manual M6 exercises the negative network path on real devices (timer-based; not headless-automated).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: docs/SETUP_IOS.md tells Pages users to skip mkcert (trusted HTTPS origin).
acceptance_criteria.verified_by: docs/SETUP_IOS.md gains a top-level blockquote fork: the public Pages deployment is already trusted HTTPS, so iOS motion works with no mkcert; the mkcert steps are scoped to the local-dev-server path only. SettingsScreen.tsx 'Laptop LAN IP' hint rewritten to say it is only needed for a local dev server.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Lint + tsc + vitest + vite build clean. Main-bundle growth budget +1 KB gzip.
acceptance_criteria.verified_by: All clean. 289/289 vitest tests (phase-6.3 baseline 271; +18: 9 buildPhoneUrl, 3 isPhoneRoute, +parsePhoneFragment role cases, 4 fitsSingleQr). Main bundle 357.05 KB / 109.84 KB gzip (baseline 356.23 / 109.46 → +0.82 KB raw / +0.38 KB gzip). PhoneApp chunk +0.07 KB gzip; PairScreen chunk +0.31 KB gzip. Under budget.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Manual real-device QA at app/verify-phase-2b5.mjs covers the Pages pair → scan → connect flow.
acceptance_criteria.verified_by: verify-phase-2b5.mjs automated gate checks C1–C4 PASS + best-effort C5 PASS, 0 console errors (artifacts/phase-2b5-verify/results.json). M1–M6 manual checklist (Pages offer-QR points at the Pages origin not a LAN IP; phone opens the same Pages URL with no hang; handshake reaches connected; commit RTT; iOS-no-mkcert; negative cross-network diagnostic) pending operator sign-off per the §B2 browser-API manual gate.

playwright_run.automated_gate_checks: C1 (hash #role=phone with no offer → phone companion manual UI), C2 (base URL with no marker → laptop app, not phone), C3 (legacy /phone path → phone companion), C4 (offer= stripped from URL, #role=phone retained) all PASS. Best-effort C5 (laptop Pair phone with LAN IP set → offer QR whose phone-url is the loopback-substituted LAN IP + #role=phone&offer=) also PASS — loopback ICE completed under headless chromium this run. Zero console errors across all five contexts.

checklist_pending_operator_sign_off: M1 — Public Pages deployment: Pair phone → offer QR within 5s; phone-url is the Pages origin (not a LAN IP) with #role=phone&offer=.
M2 — Phone (same Wi-Fi) scans → opens the SAME Pages URL → answer QR within 3s, no blank/hanging page.
M3 — Laptop scans the phone answer QR → PairScreen reaches `connected`.
M4 — Phone 'Send commit' → laptop shows 'Last commit received at +Xms'.
M5 — iOS on the Pages origin: 'Enable motion sensor' granted with NO mkcert.
M6 — Phone on mobile data / different network: no connect; ~20s later the laptop shows the `connect-timeout` same-Wi-Fi diagnostic.
manual_qa.operator_sign_off_instructions: Update artifacts/phase-2b5-verify/results.json — set each entry's `signed_off` to {date:'YYYY-MM-DD', device:'<phone model + OS/browser>'} after exercising the step against the live GitHub Pages deployment with a real phone on the same Wi-Fi. The §B2 concession requires this before the WebRTC + Pages flow is considered fully closed for real-world use; headless chromium cannot complete a real cross-device ICE handshake. M1+M2 prove the original blank-page hang is fixed from the public host; M3+M4 prove the data path; M5 proves the iOS-no-mkcert claim; M6 proves the same-LAN diagnostic and documents the accepted connectivity limitation.

gates.testing: 289/289 vitest pass (baseline 271; +18). The deployed-host buildPhoneUrl tests are the regression coverage for the original bug — they assert the QR reflects the current origin + hash role, and would fail if reverted to the `/phone`+LAN-IP shape that produced the 404/hang. isPhoneRoute, parsePhoneFragment role, fitsSingleQr (whole-URL sizing), and IPv6-loopback branch all have would-fail-if-reverted tests. The connect-timeout banner + history.replaceState strip are exercised by verify-phase-2b5.mjs C4 + the manual M6 path (timer/real-network behavior is not unit-mockable without faking timers across a component tree; covered by reasoning + manual gate).
gates.dry: isPhoneRoute + parsePhoneFragment are the single source of truth for phone-route detection and fragment parsing, consumed by both main.tsx and PhoneApp.tsx — no duplicated regex/parse. buildPhoneUrl is the single builder used by both the offer-QR path and the manual-URL helper in PairScreen. QR capacity constants live only in qr.ts.
gates.drift: No prior-phase invariants broken. Legacy /phone path detection retained (2b.1–2b.4 backward compatible). The phone offer/answer wire format, peer state machine, motion runner, calibration, and inputSource='phone' engine wiring are untouched. The Settings laptopLanIp field is unchanged in shape — only its semantics narrowed (now loopback-only) and its help copy updated.
gates.planning: Planning gate triggered (cross-layer + public-internet exposure + multiple strategies). decision-memo.md §'Phase 2b.5 — Static-host QR pairing' records the problem, the chosen hash-role design, the three rejected alternatives (404.html shim / absolute-base path / hash-role), the localhost-substitution rule, and the resolved red-team/code-review findings. phase-update.json records the plan expansion.
gates.verification_sprint: Pre-phase: 271/271 + lint + tsc + build clean at the phase-6.3 boundary (re-confirmed at start). Post-phase: 289/289 + lint + tsc + build clean; verify-phase-2b5.mjs C1–C5 PASS, 0 console errors. The full prior feature set (1–6 + 2b.1–2b.4) remains regression-covered by the unchanged suite.

review.architecture_red_team: Invoked on the design (public-internet exposure). Returned 2 blockers + 4 major + 3 minor. B1 (missing decision-memo section + dangling code citation) RESOLVED — decision-memo §'Phase 2b.5' written, citation now valid. B2 (page-loads-but-P2P-silently-fails on isolated/guest/cross networks with no TURN) RESOLVED via accepted same-LAN scope + the connect-timeout diagnostic banner + SETUP_IOS/Settings documentation. M3 (SETUP_IOS stale for Pages → mkcert unnecessary) RESOLVED via the top-level fork; the mixed-content corollary (HTTPS Pages cannot fetch http LAN endpoints; WebRTC exempt) recorded. M4 (offer SDP with private IPs on a public origin) RESOLVED via history.replaceState strip + confirmed no telemetry in the bundle + recorded no-telemetry constraint. M5 (QR sized on payload not URL) RESOLVED via fitsSingleQr/QR_MAX_URL_BYTES. M6 (peer.ts 1500ms ICE fallback weakens cross-subnet) NOTED as a pre-existing tradeoff, left unchanged (out of scope; same-LAN host candidates suffice; ICE-timing changes need real-device testing). M7 (phone reload loses role) RESOLVED — replaceState keeps #role=phone. M8 (no observability) RESOLVED by the connect-timeout banner.
review.code_reviewer: Invoked on the diff. Returned APPROVE-pending-governance (code itself sound, well-tested, tsc/eslint/tests green). Blockers were the missing decision-memo / PHASES entry / approval artifact (all now written) and a dangling §-citation (now valid). Should-fixes applied: IPv6-loopback branch test added; the documented regression coverage (deployed-host tests) is named in the testing gate above. Confirmed PASS on the items it scrutinized: base64url round-trips through `#role=phone&offer=` without URLSearchParams corruption (no +,/,= in base64url); legacy /phone backward compat; loopback-vs-deployed + missing-IP + trailing-slash/index.html + port handling; no new phone-hang path; DRY (single parsing source).
review.qa_playwright: User-visible surface gated by verify-phase-2b5.mjs C1–C5 (all PASS, 0 console errors) plus the M1–M6 manual checklist under the §B2 browser-API concession. The cross-device WebRTC handshake from the live Pages origin cannot be exercised headlessly (no real UDP/STUN path between two real devices); manual operator sign-off is the authoritative gate for that path.

suggested_commit_message: phase-2b.5: static-host QR pairing — origin+hash-role URL, connect diagnostic, QR-size + offer-privacy hardening
